drills.q: Compute Grover's optimal iteration count and success probability for N=64, M=1.
drills.a: theta = arcsin(1/8) ~ 0.1253 rad; k ~ pi*8/4 = 6 iterations (floor/round); success = sin^2(13*theta) ~ 0.9995. Formula: k ~ (pi/4)sqrt(N).

drills.q: Why does DJ need the ancilla in |-> rather than |0>?
drills.a: U_f XORs f(x) into |y>. With y=|->, X|-> = -|->, so the XOR becomes a phase (-1)^f(x) on the control register (kickback) without collapsing anything; with |0> you'd just entangle data with ancilla bits and lose the interference pattern.

drills.q: A colleague claims a 2026 hardware demo 'ran Shor'. What follow-ups separate honest claim from hype?
drills.a: Ask: what N was factored (15? 21?), was the period hard-coded or compiled away, logical or physical qubits, error mitigation used. Full Shor for real keys needs millions of physical qubits in fault-tolerant mode; demos verify compilers/control, not threat.

drills.q: Give the two-line business answer to 'when do we need PQC done by?'.
drills.a: 1) Data confidentiality horizon > ~2033 means encrypt with PQC now because of harvest-now-decrypt-later. 2) Signatures/certificates can migrate later but inventory and vendor pressure should start immediately since enterprise migrations take 2-5 years against CNSA-2.0/NIST timelines of 2027-2035.

drills.q: Why is there no Grover-style win to be had over a B-tree index lookup?
drills.a: Grover needs black-box oracle access and unstructured search; an index exploits structure to answer in O(log n) comparisons already, beating sqrt(N) asymptotically, and quantum memory access costs would erase constants. Quantum search only wins when nothing better than linear scan exists classically.

drills.q: In Shor, why measure register 2 at all before the QFT?
drills.a: Measuring g^x mod N collapses register 1 onto {x : g^x = c}, i.e., an exact arithmetic progression with spacing r - which is what the QFT reads out. Skipping it works too (the QFT acts on both registers), but measuring is simpler and loses nothing: the progression structure is identical.

drills.q: Your Grover demo on hardware returns near-uniform counts. Three diagnosis steps?
drills.a: 1) Check post-transpile depth vs coherence budget (oracle Toffolis inflate depth). 2) Verify iteration count matches M and N (wrong k overshoots back down toward uniform). 3) Inspect qubit ordering/oracle sign conventions between simulator and ISA.

drills.q: Rank speedup quality: DJ (exponential query), Grover (quadratic), Shor (exponential structural). Which transfers to practice and why?
drills.a: Shor transfers: exponential AND applies to real deployed cryptanalysis (RSA/ECC) since inputs are natural numbers, not promised oracles. DJ's exponential is promise-artificial; Grover is real but quadratic and mostly eaten by fault-tolerance constants outside crypto. Structure beats raw exponent when inputs are natural.

drills.q: State the continued-fraction step precisely enough to implement.
drills.a: From measured c/Q with gcd(c,Q)=1, expand c/Q as continued fractions; take convergents k'/r' with r' < N; test each r' via g^{r'} == 1 mod N; first hit gives order r. Success needs gcd(k,r)=1 which happens with probability phi(r)/r.

drills.q: What single sentence kills 'quantum breaks all encryption' panic in a design review?
drills.a: Shor breaks public-key (RSA/ECC) but Grover only halves symmetric strength, so AES-256 + SHA-384 survive while key exchange and signatures migrate to ML-KEM/ML-DSA per FIPS 203/204.
